transcript.content: Hello. Welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’ve started having these beliefs that something is going on behind the scenes at work, and even when people tell me it’s not true, I just can’t shake the feeling. I finally agreed to come in because I feel like I’m losing track of what’s real and what’s just in my head.
Along with these thoughts, have you also been hearing any voices or seeing things that other people don't seem to notice?

I don't see anything, but I have been hearing a voice. Usually, when I'm alone in my apartment after a shift, this low male voice will calmly comment on what I'm doing—like saying "you messed that up" when I'm trying to check my sales numbers.
Alongside these voices and beliefs, have you been experiencing any major shifts in your mood, such as feeling deeply depressed or, on the other hand, unusually energetic and high?

Yes, I've been feeling deeply depressed, like there's a heavy gray filter over everything and I've lost interest in cooking or seeing my friends. I never feel high or unusually energetic; at best, my energy picked up slightly to a normal level for a brief time last summer, but I've never felt manic.
Have you ever experienced these voices or beliefs during times when your mood was completely normal and you weren't feeling depressed?

Yes, late last summer my energy briefly picked up and I didn't feel as depressed, but the voices and beliefs didn't go away. For about two weeks straight, I still clearly heard that low voice in my apartment and was convinced my coworkers were running those experiments on me.
How long have you been experiencing these voices and beliefs in total, and during how much of that time have you also felt depressed?

The voices and the suspicious feelings at work have been going on for roughly a year and a few months now. I've felt heavy and depressed for most of that same time—for a little over a year—so the low mood has definitely been there for the majority of this whole period.
To help me understand your low mood better, have you also noticed other changes during those depressed periods, such as shifts in your sleep, appetite, energy levels, or concentration?

My appetite has completely dropped off, and I've lost enough weight that my work pants are slipping off my hips. My concentration is also shot—I feel foggy, have to read simple tickets multiple times, and my body and thoughts feel slowed down like I'm moving underwater.
Along with the low mood and concentration issues, have you also been experiencing any changes in your sleep patterns, or feelings of extreme worthlessness or guilt?

I constantly feel like a burden to everyone, replaying small mistakes at work and old family arguments in my head and thinking the restaurant would run smoother and my sister wouldn't have to worry if I weren't here. I haven't really noticed any major changes in my sleep, as those heavy feelings of guilt and worthlessness are what really weigh on me.
During those two weeks last summer when your energy picked up, did your feelings of depression, guilt, and low appetite go away completely, or were they just less intense?

They actually went away completely during those two weeks—I didn't feel down at all, and my appetite returned to normal. But even though I felt emotionally okay, the voice in my apartment and the belief that my coworkers were testing me continued just as clearly.
Have you been using any recreational drugs, alcohol, or new medications regularly, or do you have any physical medical conditions?
No, I don't use any recreational drugs or alcohol, and I'm not on any new medications. I also don't have any physical medical conditions that I know of.

The presence of a 2-week period where mood symptoms fully resolved but psychotic symptoms persisted helps rule out a primary mood disorder with psychotic features (F32.3/F33.3). The differential remains between Schizophrenia (F20) and Schizoaffective disorder, depressive type (F25), and sufficient history has been gathered to make this diagnostic distinction.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets the criteria for Schizoaffective Disorder (F25). They present with concurrent symptoms of schizophrenia (auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions) and a major depressive episode. The depressive symptoms have been present for the majority of the total duration of the illness (over 1 year out of 1 year and 3 months). Crucially, the patient experienced a two-week period last summer where the mood symptoms resolved completely but the psychotic symptoms (hallucinations and delusions) persisted, satisfying the requirement for at least 2 weeks of psychotic symptoms in the absence of a major mood episode.
